name: Pansy Division
label: Lookout!
lede: Two guys, a want ad in the San Francisco Weekly, and a thirty-year plan to be the loud, funny, unapologetic gay band rock never had.

eras.title: An ad in the paper
eras.text: Jon Ginoli starts as a solo act, then answers his own want ad with a band. The goal is simple and, in rock, unheard of: a group of gay men singing about gay sex and gay romance without a wink or a disguise.

years.h: [[Jon Ginoli|a6969636-a63a-456f-90fe-82bf59078154]] records a first cassette of Pansy Division songs
years.p: The 1991 tape was cut in Champaign, Illinois with bassist Chris Bowe, and nine of its tracks later land on the debut album.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, the material on Undressed was recorded between July 1991 and August 1992, and the earliest sessions were the independent cassette with a different line-up.

years.cap: Pansy Division in San Francisco, early 1990s
years.h: An ad for gay musicians into the Ramones and Buzzcocks
years.p: Ginoli places a notice in the San Francisco Weekly. [[Chris Freeman|8853ba49-6415-4730-8c6b-7f90a015f065]] answers, and with drummer Jay Paget they become what they call the first entirely out gay rock band.
years.xp:
The ad asked for gay musicians into the Ramones, Buzzcocks and early Beatles. Freeman joined on bass and vocals and stayed for the whole run.

Ginoli, who had been involved with ACT UP in San Francisco, has said he wanted to be the gay band that actually sang about it.

eras.title: Lookout! and the Green Day summer
eras.text: Signed to Berkeley's Lookout! Records, the band puts out a record a year and lands on the biggest punk tour of 1994, playing to teenagers who came for someone else.

years.h: Undressed is out on Lookout!
years.p: The debut is thirty-three minutes of crunchy, explicit pop-punk. AllMusic singled out the Byrds-flavored "Boyfriend Wanted".
years.xp: Trouser Press said the band's lyrics cut right to the chase. Robert Christgau gave it a one-star honorable mention. Thirty years later, Lookout!'s Larry Livermore and the cover model Alex Fazekas-Paul joined an anniversary interview series, and the album was first in a run of remastered vinyl reissues.

years.h: Deflowered pairs raunch with safer-sex advice
years.p: The second album mixes sex songs with pieces about the AIDS crisis. Ginoli put condom instructions and youth resources in the liner notes.
years.xp: Ginoli told Xtra the band felt they had to give more information, not just jokes. The record's title later became the name of his memoir.
play: Fem in a Black Leather Jacket

years.h: Touring with [[Green Day|084308bd-1654-436f-ba03-df6697104e19]] at the height of Dookie
years.p: Lookout! labelmates Green Day take Pansy Division out for several months, in front of thousands of high school kids a night.
years.xp: Ginoli says the crowds were not the older, gay-friendly audience he expected, and calls it an amazing opportunity they never expected to have. In New York, Howard Stern met the band backstage and talked about them on his radio show, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: Pile Up includes "Smells Like Queer Spirit"
years.p: The third album includes that song, plus a version of "Cowboys Are Frequently, Secretly Fond of Each Other".
years.xp: Both covers are listed on the album by Wikipedia. The band also made underwear photo cards and trading cards for a 1995 tour of eastern Canada.

years.h: Trading cards and underwear photos on a Canadian tour
years.p: On a 1995 eastern Canada run, Pansy Division handed out underwear photography and trading cards of the band as promotion.

eras.title: A new drummer, a video on MTV
eras.text: A steady rhythm section and a second guitarist turn a duo-plus-hired-hands band into a real touring unit. The songs also grow more serious.

years.h: [[Luis Illades|cc520ad0-376d-4ce0-bfc0-6f310187e72d]] joins on drums for good
years.p: Illades becomes the permanent drummer in 1996, ending a run of changing drummers, and is still in the band.

years.h: Wish I'd Taken Pictures gets "I Really Wanted You" on MTV
years.p: The video for the single "I Really Wanted You" aired on MTV, per Wikipedia, a rare spot for an openly gay punk band.

years.h: Patrick Goodwin joins on guitar
years.p: Goodwin adds a lead guitar to the line-up and stays until 2004.

years.h: More Lovin' From Our Oven collects the B-sides
years.p: Lookout! puts out a compilation of rarities and B-sides from the first years.

years.h: Absurd Pop Song Romance turns toward heartache
years.p: The last Lookout! album is more mature and romantic, and drops much of the early jokey raunch.

years.h: Opening for [[Rancid|24f8d8a5-269b-475c-a1cb-792990b0b2ee]] on the Life Won't Wait tour
years.p: The band opens for the Bay Area punk veterans on the tour for the 1998 album Life Won't Wait.

eras.title: Alternative Tentacles, and a slower pace
eras.text: With Lookout! winding down, the band moves to Jello Biafra's label, records a new album, and members drift to different cities.

years.h: Total Entertainment! arrives on Alternative Tentacles
years.p: The first record on [[Jello Biafra|2280ca0e-6968-4349-8c36-cb0cbd6ee95f]]'s label balances humor with sharper songwriting.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the album to 2003, though the band's own bio says 2000. Activity slowed afterwards, and the group mostly played pride festivals and local shows.

years.h: Joel Reader takes over on lead guitar
years.p: Reader, who joined in 2004, replaces Goodwin after a brief stint from temporary guitarist Bernard Yin.

years.h: The Essential Pansy Division: 30 tracks and a DVD
years.p: Alternative Tentacles collects the career so far, with video and concert footage.

eras.title: Films, a memoir, a fresh record
eras.text: Nearly two decades in, the band gets its own documentary and Ginoli's book, and keeps touring.

years.h: National tour with the [[Avengers|f290c284-cc49-49a6-bc89-3f58de0c40ed]]
years.p: The first big national run since 2003 pairs the band with the reformed San Francisco punk band.

years.h: Pansy Division: Life in a Gay Rock Band hits the festivals
years.p: Michael Carmona's documentary tours LGBT film festivals internationally, and comes out on DVD in 2009.

years.h: Ginoli publishes Deflowered: My Life in Pansy Division
years.p: The memoir comes out on Cleis Press.

years.h: That's So Gay brings the noise back
years.p: The album returns to raucous energy, and comes with a live DVD.

years.h: Quite Contrary marks 25 years
years.p: Recorded in 2015, the album leads with the single "Blame the Bible" and is followed by tours of both coasts.

eras.title: Nine hundred and something shows
eras.text: A younger, queerer audience finds them, and the band chases a round number.

years.h: Featured in Queercore: How to Punk a Revolution
years.p: Yony Leyser's documentary places Pansy Division in the history of the scene.

years.h: Mosswood Meltdown, opening for Bikini Kill
years.p: The band plays Oakland's Mosswood Meltdown festival, opening for [[Bikini Kill|1397d045-1603-41fc-80b9-712c18360145]].

years.h: Opening for The B-52s at Mosswood
years.p: The band returns to Mosswood Meltdown, this time supporting The B-52s.

years.h: Show number 1,000, in San Francisco
years.p: On April 19, 2025 in San Francisco, Pansy Division reach their long-time goal of playing 1,000 shows.
years.xp: The band suggested this may be their final touring cycle. Ginoli and Freeman, both from the original 1991 line-up, are still in the group with Illades and Reader.
